item.content:encoded: I really like this spot! It has an awesome garden out back, and the building itself has a lot of charm. I’ve been here a few time with big groups and it’s always been a good time, and the appetizers are good, especially the Spinach and Artichoke Toasted Ravioli.

item.title: Seamus McDaniel's
item.description: Seamus McDaniel's feels like a pretty standard Irish bar and grill to me. I like that they have an outdoor patio area, but their food was just very standard,…
item.content:encoded: Seamus McDaniel’s feels like a pretty standard Irish bar and grill to me. I like that they have an outdoor patio area, but their food was just very standard, and they don’t really have anything Irish themed on the menu, unless you count a Reuben. I’m personally just not the biggest fan of bar food, but overall it’s a good spot to hang out at.

item.title: Tee Rak Thai
item.description: Tucked into a street along Shaw you'll find Tee Rak Thai, a traditional regional Thai restaurant. "Tee Rak" means "My Love" in Thai, and you can definitely…
item.content:encoded:
Tucked into a street along Shaw you’ll find Tee Rak Thai, a traditional regional Thai restaurant. “Tee Rak” means “My Love” in Thai, and you can definitely feel the love that goes into this homemade cuisine.

I tried Moo Ping, which are BBQ Pork Skewers, and potstickers, along with one of my favorite beverages, Thai Tea. The tea was good and the potstickers were very crispy.

For the entrees, I tried Pad Kee Mao (drunken noodles) and Pad See Ew, two common Thai classics. Both were great, with proper thick noodles and flavor infused all throughout. I got it with crispy pork belly which was the special of the day; if I ordered it again, I would probably try chicken or beef, because the crispy pork belly was so rich, but it was tasty.

I really liked the spice level (I chose 2 out of 4). Usually it’s not spicy enough for me at that level and this had a very pleasant level of spice.

The building is also a classic St. Louis red brick (as is most of Shaw) with some nice decor.

item.title: Pizzeria da Gloria
item.description: Everything about Pizzeria da Gloria is amazing. The vibe is welcoming, the patio is beautiful, and the food is top notch and reasonably priced for everything…
item.content:encoded:
Everything about Pizzeria da Gloria is amazing. The vibe is welcoming, the patio is beautiful, and the food is top notch and reasonably priced for everything you get. Pizzeria da Gloria, along with Louie, is the best Italian food I’ve had in St. Louis.

I particularly loved the caprese salad - made with homemade mozzarella! - but the meatballs were too good to not choose them as “my pick”. Probably the best meatballs I’ve ever had.

Let’s not forget the Neapolitan-style pizza, made in an enormous wood-fired oven. My only issue was that the Margherita pizza I ordered was more of a regular cheese pizza, since it didn’t use fresh tomatoes and mozzarella slices, but it was still delicious.

This is the perfect spot to get a nice birthday dinner or other small celebration.

item.title: Dalie's Smokehouse
item.description: I think Dalie's is currently my favorite spot for BBQ in St. Louis. The smoked wings are fantastic, and the ribs are fantastic. And although the brisket is not…
item.content:encoded: I think Dalie’s is currently my favorite spot for BBQ in St. Louis. The smoked wings are fantastic, and the ribs are fantastic. And although the brisket is not my favorite - Texas-style - it is still incredibly tender and flavorful. The service is also excellent at this spot.

item.title: Taqueria Hectorito
item.description: Taqueria Hectorito, which is connected to the El Torito grocery store, is an outdoor Mexican grill and patio on Cherokee St. Of all the taco spots I've eaten…
item.content:encoded:
Taqueria Hectorito, which is connected to the El Torito grocery store, is an outdoor Mexican grill and patio on Cherokee St.

Of all the taco spots I’ve eaten at so far, this one most closely resembles some of the restaurants I’ve been to in central Mexico.

When I visited, I tried steak, al pastor, and carnitas tacos. The salsas were spicy and flavorful, and I was definitely impressed by the quality and freshness of the onion, cilantro, and radish toppings, and the tortillas were cooked really well. I just wasn’t a big fan of the meat in the tacos, so overall it isn’t one of my favorite spots, but it was cool to hang out at an outdoor patio along the street in the main Mexican district of the city.

item.title: Mom's Deli
item.description: I'm fortunate enough to have tried Mom's Deli at its original, iconic location before it got relocated to the Hampton strip. Mom's Deli is a classic St. Louis…
item.content:encoded:
I’m fortunate enough to have tried Mom’s Deli at its original, iconic location before it got relocated to the Hampton strip. Mom’s Deli is a classic St. Louis institution, and I understand a lot of people have been going here for their whole life and have strong feelings about it.

Personally, Mom’s Deli isn’t really the spot for me - I’d rather go to Blues City Deli or The Gramophone for a more upscale sandwich experience, but an everyday sandwich it’s alright.

It starts with homemade crust, St. Louis smooth and slightly sweet sauce and a St. Louis cheese blend!”. I’m not sure I’m sold on that, I haven’t been a fan of Provel on thick crust pizzas, but I will definitely try it at some point.

item.content:encoded: St. Louis is a sandwich town, and The Gramophone adds to that reputation. The fact that you can get a sandwich this good in a bar late at night is pretty spectacular. Highly recommended!

item.title: Faraci Pizza
item.description: Faraci Pizza is one of the original Pizza spots in St. Louis. It began in Ferguson, Missouri in 1968, and moved to Ellisville in West County in the '90s. Due…
item.content:encoded:
Faraci Pizza is one of the original Pizza spots in St. Louis. It began in Ferguson, Missouri in 1968, and moved to Ellisville in West County in the ’90s. Due to its original location, it has that “North side” St. Louis-style pizza vibe. The pizza is rectangular, and the crust is a bit more thick and stable than some other spots, while still being a crispy cracker-crust.

At Faraci, they make the meatballs and sausage from scratch, and use sliced Provel instead of shredded cheese or a blend.

Faraci is very much a favorite neighborhood joint for the surrounding area, and it can get busy during holidays (I’ve seen them just disconnect the phone due to too many callers).

item.title: Park Avenue Coffee
item.description: Park Avenue is a local coffee chain that has locations in Lafayette Square, The Hill, Midtown, and Downtown. They also make one of the better gooey butter…
item.content:encoded:
Park Avenue is a local coffee chain that has locations in Lafayette Square, The Hill, Midtown, and Downtown. They also make one of the better gooey butter cakes around town.

The coffee from Park Avenue is the best - I order it as my regular, daily coffee. It is much less acidic than most other coffee roasters, and they have some nice, subtle flavored coffees like cinnamon hazelnut and southern pecan.

item.title: Carondelet
item.description: Carondelet is an interesting part of St. Louis that was originally its own city that was annexed by St. Louis in 1870 (one of the last that ever would be!).…
item.content:encoded:
Carondelet is an interesting part of St. Louis that was originally its own city that was annexed by St. Louis in 1870 (one of the last that ever would be!). It’s a very old, very French village from back in the day.

I didn’t really know there was anything in Carondelet aside from Stacked (burgers) and Sugarwitch (ice cream sandwiches) when I first moved here, but I discovered there’s a whole strip of bars along the riverfront. Most of St. Louis does not have residential areas or restaurants along the riverfront as it’s mostly been historically used for industry, so it’s interesting to see a riverfront neighborhood along the southern edge.

Many locals refer to this whole area as Carondelet, but it’s officially two city neighborhoods, Carondelet and Patch. Historically, Patch was part of Carondelet City before it the whole area was annexed by St. Louis. Much of the retail corridor is in Patch, but a lot of those places refer to themselves as being in Carondelet, such as Stacked. Due to the amount of cultural overlap I’ve included both Carondelet and Patch together in this article, although both are unique entities.

item.title: Clayton
item.description: Clayton is one of the commercial and financial districts of St. Louis, and contains its own bustling downtown. It's located immediately to the west of Forest…
item.content:encoded: Clayton is one of the commercial and financial districts of St. Louis, and contains its own bustling downtown. It’s located immediately to the west of Forest Park, and is centrally located relative to most things to do between St. Louis and the County. It’s an upscale and highly sought after suburb with abundant green space that is studded with grandiose mansions all throughout.

item.title: Kirkwood
item.description: Kirkwood is an affluent suburb with a walkable downtown area. You'll find a Clementine's, the local ice cream chain, A 4Hands brewery, and Citizen Kane's, a…
item.content:encoded: Kirkwood is an affluent suburb with a walkable downtown area. You’ll find a Clementine’s, the local ice cream chain, A 4Hands brewery, and Citizen Kane’s, a popular local steakhouse. There’s also a local Lego resale shop called The Minifig Shop, along with other small shops and boutiques.

item.title: Maplewood
item.description: Maplewood is the first inner-ring suburb you'll encounter after going west past Dogtown and Lindenwood Park. One notable feature is the backward Maplewood sign…
item.content:encoded:
Maplewood is the first inner-ring suburb you’ll encounter after going west past Dogtown and Lindenwood Park. One notable feature is the backward Maplewood sign made up of reclaimed items that signifies your entrance or exit from Maplewood. It’s meant to appear correctly in the rear-view as you drive away from it, but it definitely looks like Doowelpam when you drive towards it.

The main strip along Manchester is lively and full of restaurants, bars, breweries, and small businesses.

item.title: Midtown
item.description: Midtown is an area between Downtown and Forest Park that is seeing a lot of growth right now. One of the biggest draws of the area is the City Foundry, a food…
item.content:encoded:
Midtown is an area between Downtown and Forest Park that is seeing a lot of growth right now. One of the biggest draws of the area is the City Foundry, a food hall and market built into a restored vacant foundry building, and The Cortex Innovation Community, a tech hub in St. Louis providing a coworking and office space for startups and businesses.

Just north is Grand Center, the theatre and arts district.

I’m hopeful about the innovation projects that are being implemented to help stimulate the economy and add more energy and vibrancy to the city. Between the office spaces, the food halls and other dining, there’s a lot going on in Midtown.

There is also Midtown Alley, consisting of some businesses and breweries along Locust St.

item.title: Shaw
item.description: Shaw is a popular, centrally located neighborhood in St. Louis that is highly residential with a few restaurants, bars, and cafes interspersed. There's Ice's…
item.content:encoded:
Shaw is a popular, centrally located neighborhood in St. Louis that is highly residential with a few restaurants, bars, and cafes interspersed. There’s Ice’s Plain & Fancy, a Nitro ice cream parlor, and Sasha’s on Shaw, a wine and cheese bar, both of which give the neighborhood an upscale, family friendly feel. Down the center of the neighborhood is a boulevard with historic houses and mature tree canopy.

Along the western edge of the neighborhood is the Tower Grove Connector, a two-way, protected bike path that goes north to Vandeventer and will connect with the Brickline Greenway. I found this path to be delightful and a great example of a modern urban improvement.

item.title: Soulard
item.description: Soulard is known as the bar and nightlife part of town. It's the oldest residential neighborhood in St. Louis, and has kept much of its original character…
item.content:encoded:
Soulard is known as the bar and nightlife part of town. It’s the oldest residential neighborhood in St. Louis, and has kept much of its original character intact. There are many small, winding streets with bars, restaurants, clubs, cafes, and live music dotted throughout.

Unfortunately, a large highway runs right through the neighborhood, as the whole area was seen as poor and obsolete and was planned for demolition after World War II, to be replaced with the more modern suburban homes and car-centric layouts we see almost everywhere else. Fortunately, enough people who cared prevented this from happening and Soulard got placed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1972, but the highway that runs through still prevents it from reaching its full potential.

item.title: Southampton
item.description: Southampton is a charming neighborhood close to many bars and restaurants all along Hampton Ave, such as Mom's Deli, J.J. Twig's, Salvage Yard, and Salt &…
item.content:encoded: Southampton is a charming neighborhood close to many bars and restaurants all along Hampton Ave, such as Mom’s Deli, J.J. Twig’s, Salvage Yard, and Salt & Smoke BBQ. The area is affectionately known as “SOHA”. There are many styles of brick-built homes in Southampton have a lot of character. It’s a quiet neighborhood close to Francis Park in St. Louis Hills, and also not too far from Tower Grove Park.

item.title: St. Louis Hills
item.description: The tagline for St. Louis Hills was "Country living in the City" when the neighborhood was first developed. There are the "St. Louis Hills Estates" on the…
item.content:encoded:
The tagline for St. Louis Hills was “Country living in the City” when the neighborhood was first developed. There are the “St. Louis Hills Estates” on the southern end of the neighborhood, which are traditional-style large suburban lots and homes, and the rest of St. Louis Hills, which are more traditional style homes that all circle around Francis Park.

During Christmas, a St. Louis tradition is to go get frozen custard at Ted Drewes then walk down Candy Cane Lane, a strip of homes in St. Louis Hills that go all-out with Christmas decorations.

St. Louis Hills is one of the more suburban-esque neighborhoods in the city. It is as far to the south west in the city as you can get, but not too far from the main commercial strip on Hampton, and another along Route 66 where Ted Drewes and LeGrand’s Market is.

The proximity of all the homes along Francis Park and Willmore Park gives the residents ample green space, and it’s not far from Maplewood and Webster Groves to the west.

item.title: Tower Grove South
item.description: Tower Grove South is the aptly named neighborhood just south of Tower Grove Park. The area is largely residential with two main business strips - one near the…
item.content:encoded:
Tower Grove South is the aptly named neighborhood just south of Tower Grove Park. The area is largely residential with two main business strips - one near the western edge along Morganford Rd, and one on the eastern edge along South Grand Blvd. There are a few cafes and bars scattered around the rest of the neighborhood.

Along Grand, you’ll find a wide variety of international restaurants, from Brazilian and Mexican to Indian, Persian, and Lebanese, to Thai, Vietnamese, and Cantonese. There is also Apotheosis Comics, a local comic store, and Dunaway Books, a local used bookstore.

item.title: Webster Groves
item.description: Webster Groves is a charming, upscale suburb with two main walkable strips. On the west end, you have Telva at the Ridge, a Balkan-inspired cafe from the…
item.content:encoded: Webster Groves is a charming, upscale suburb with two main walkable strips. On the west end, you have Telva at the Ridge, a Balkan-inspired cafe from the owners of Balkan Treat Box, and Olive + Oak, an intimate and upscale restaurant and cocktail bar. On the east end, you have Balkan Treat Box on a strip with multiple small, locally owned bookstores, some cafes, and Webster University.

item.title: Bono's Pizzeria
item.description: I'm particular about deep dish, and I was highly impressed with both the Chicago deep dish pizza and the St. Louis-style pizza at Bono's Pizzeria on Hampton.…
item.content:encoded:
I’m particular about deep dish, and I was highly impressed with both the Chicago deep dish pizza and the St. Louis-style pizza at Bono’s Pizzeria on Hampton. The St. Louis style had a crisp, almost tavern-style pizza like quality to it, and the deep dish was incredibly authentic.

The deep dish at Bono’s is my second favorite deep dish - Lou Malnati’s being my favorite. Bono’s does a similar style, with a fresh, chunky tomato sauce on top and a crisp, almost pie-like crust. The only thing that puts Lou’s over the top for me is the entire sausage disc they use. I like Bono’s more than Pequod’s, and significantly more than Giordano’s or Gino’s East.

This is a great spot!

item.title: Bevo Mill
item.description: In the 1990s, St. Louis was one of the cities that the government chose to place refugees of the Bosnian War. Bevo Mill in particular was one of the main areas…
item.content:encoded:
In the 1990s, St. Louis was one of the cities that the government chose to place refugees of the Bosnian War. Bevo Mill in particular was one of the main areas where they settled, and there are many Balkan restaurants, delis, and butchers along the main strip on Gravois as a result.

The Bosnians who came to St. Louis helped shape the neighborhood into what it is today, and St. Louis remains one of the largest Bosnian communities in the United States. The area of Bevo Mill in particular is no longer the epicenter of the Bosnian population, as many have moved to the surrounding county areas.

One large defining feature of the neighborhood is Das Bevo, a large German beer hall right at the Bevo Windmill.

item.title: Central West End
item.description: Central West End is an upscale urban neighborhood in St. Louis city. It sits right along Forest Park and has a walkable downtown vibe. It's the biggest and…
item.content:encoded:
Central West End is an upscale urban neighborhood in St. Louis city. It sits right along Forest Park and has a walkable downtown vibe. It’s the biggest and most populated neighborhood in the city, and is often recommended for new transplants.

It’s also home to Up-Down Arcade, an arcade full of retro games, craft beers, and a pizza window.

When you’re in Central West End, you’ll see people walking around and sitting at outdoor cafes and restaurants, or visiting the various book stores and boutique stores. I think Central West End is competing with Downtown as “the place to be” for tourists, transplants, and residents.

item.title: Delmar Loop
item.description: The Delmar Loop, often referred to as just The Loop, is a commercial strip that straddles the western edge of St. Louis city and the east end of University…
item.content:encoded:
The Delmar Loop, often referred to as just The Loop, is a commercial strip that straddles the western edge of St. Louis city and the east end of University City. It was named “One of the 10 Great Streets in America” by The American Planning Association in 2007 due the “sustained efforts of local business, government, and the community to achieve successful physical and economic revitalization.”

There are a lot of notable features in the area that distinguish it from other parts of the city, such as a Walk of Fame of famous St. Louisans, and the Loop Trolley that passes through the neighborhood and ferries people to Forest Park.

The Pageant and Delmar Hall are two back-to-back concert halls that host many of the bands and artists that pass through St. Louis. The Loop is also a big part of the restaurant scene of St. Louis. There is a large representation of Asian cuisine in the area as well, including Corner 17 and my personal favorite, Kishimoto Mendo.

item.title: Dogtown
item.description: Dogtown is an unofficial neighborhood made up of four city neighborhoods: Cheltenham, Clayton-Tamm, Franz Park, and Hi-Pointe, and also consists of part of one…
item.content:encoded: Dogtown is an unofficial neighborhood made up of four city neighborhoods: Cheltenham, Clayton-Tamm, Franz Park, and Hi-Pointe, and also consists of part of one additional area called Ellendale. Dogtown sits just south of Forest Park and mostly north of Manchester Rd. It is historically the Irish neighborhood in St. Louis, and hosts a St. Patrick’s Day parade.

item.title: Downtown
item.description: As a kid, I can remember crossing over the Mississippi river into St. Louis on road trips out west and saying, "Hey look, it's the Arch!" No matter where you…
item.content:encoded:
As a kid, I can remember crossing over the Mississippi river into St. Louis on road trips out west and saying, “Hey look, it’s the Arch!” No matter where you are in St. Louis, you can probably see the Arch looming in the distance. The Arch is the biggest and most impressive monument in St. Louis, one of the most recognizable American monuments, and the biggest tourist activity to in Downtown St. Louis.

One of my favorite places in St. Louis is City Museum. Calling it a “museum” gives the wrong impression for what it is - a giant concrete playground for both kids and adults. It’s hard to describe without experiencing it, and I think if anyone only visits St. Louis one time, City Museum should be on their list.

Downtown is the main area visitors and tourists will see when visiting St. Louis, but many come away with a negative opinion of the city. The area does not have the most vibrant energy, and is mostly emptied out after working hours. Downtown is still working on finding its identity in a rapidly shifting economy, but at a slower rate than any other city in America.

item.title: The Grove
item.description: The Grove is the LGBTQ district in St. Louis, and is home to a strip of local restaurants and bars, located in the Forest Park Southeast neighborhood. It's…
item.content:encoded:
The Grove is the LGBTQ district in St. Louis, and is home to a strip of local restaurants and bars, located in the Forest Park Southeast neighborhood.

It’s also the only district in St. Louis that has a cute little neon entry sign. I’m a big fan of this sign, as it reminds me of all the signs around neighborhoods in San Diego. I genuinely hope more neighborhood strips in St. Louis add them, though I’m not sure where else would be a contender. Maybe Cherokee St., DeMun, or the Delmar Loop.

The Grove was one of the first places in St. Louis I was introduced to, as I had met up with some coworkers at The Gramophone, a popular sandwich shop. I’ve also been to Urban Chestnut, which is a brewery with a great vibe. (I went to both of these before I started paying attention to the food enough, so I’ll have to revisit before I make entries for those spots in the Food map).

A few of my favorite restaurants in the city are in the Grove. I think Sultan is one of the best Middle Eastern restaurants around. Grace Meat and Three was a good fried chicken spot, and Pie Guy was the best New York-style pizza I’ve had, but unfortunately they both closed.

item.title: The Hill
item.description: The Hill is the Italian-American neighborhood in St. Louis. It has been called America's Last Little Italy. The neighborhood is fiercely proud of its Italian…
item.content:encoded:
The Hill is the Italian-American neighborhood in St. Louis. It has been called America’s Last Little Italy. The neighborhood is fiercely proud of its Italian heritage, with Italian flag banners posted all throughout the neighborhood, and fire hydrants and crosswalks painted in the Italian colors.

The neighborhood’s slogan is “Improve, not move”, part of community outreach efforts to improve the neighborhood and homes within. This has encouraged people to stay and build instead of moving away and letting the area stagnate, which has been very successful for the area.

There’s a nice mix of restaurants, delis, cafes, breweries, and other businesses intertwined with the homes in the neighborhood, making it a pleasant place to walk around. There are a few well-known, nice Italian restaurants such as Charlie Gitto’s, Anthonino’s Taverna, and Mama’s on the Hill. Of course, my favorite pizza club in the city, Nicky Slices Pizza Club is there, too.

I appreciate that there’s hardly a chain restaurant in sight in the neighborhood, and there’s a good amount of energy, with people sitting at outdoor cafes and walking around.

The real estate of the neighborhood consists of a lot of very small, brick-built shotgun style homes, with some newer builds beginning to pop up.

item.title: Sultan
item.description: This is our go-to spot for Middle Eastern food. Specifically, the beef kefta kabob is flavorful, tender, juicy, and just fantastic. Everything else is good,…
item.content:encoded:
This is our go-to spot for Middle Eastern food. Specifically, the beef kefta kabob is flavorful, tender, juicy, and just fantastic. Everything else is good, too - the saffron rice garnished with pomegranate, the spiced lentil soup topped with cracked black pepper, and especially the baba ganoush, my favorite in the city.

Water, tea, and beverages are served in traditional Turkish style cups and carafes, which adds a nice touch. The ambiance is great and the place has been full every time I’ve visited, and the food has been incredibly fresh. They also have a mint lemonade that is the perfect balance of mint, lemon, and sweetness.

This is one of my absolute top spots in the city, it has been consistently delightful on every visit.

item.title: Tikka Tangy
item.description: Tikka Tangy is great for when you want a cozy night in with samosas and Butter Chicken or Chicken Tikka Masala. The curry is flavorful, rich, and consistently…
item.content:encoded:
Tikka Tangy is great for when you want a cozy night in with samosas and Butter Chicken or Chicken Tikka Masala. The curry is flavorful, rich, and consistently good.

They also have pizzas, which I haven’t tried, and some Middle Eastern dishes like shawarma and hummus, which I have tried and thought it was just okay. I usually stick to the Indian dishes at Tikka Tangy.

item.title: Anthonino's Taverna
item.description: Anthonino's Taverna is an Italian and Greek restaurant on the Hill. It was once featured on Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives with Guy Fieri, particularly for the…
item.content:encoded: Anthonino’s Taverna is an Italian and Greek restaurant on the Hill. It was once featured on Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives with Guy Fieri, particularly for the toasted ravioli.

item.title: Blues City Deli
item.description: Blues City Deli is an absolute gem of a spot. You can expect to see a line when you go to visit, but you'll get to check out all the Blues memorabilia,…
item.content:encoded:
Blues City Deli is an absolute gem of a spot. You can expect to see a line when you go to visit, but you’ll get to check out all the Blues memorabilia, portraits, and concert posters while you wait.

So far, I’ve tried the roast beef and the reuben sandwiches. The reuben is made with house-smoked pastrami, and is the best I’ve had so far. I’d rate Blues City Deli as one of the best restaurants in the entire St. Louis area. It even topped the list in 2023 in one of the Yelp Top 100 lists.

I’d like to work my way through the entire menu, because everything has been so good. I also have to get around to trying the Italian beef and updating with my thoughts, as it’s not easy to find Italian Beef in St. Louis.

Blues City Deli is definitely on my “must-try” spots in St. Louis.

item.title: Bud's Pizza & Beer
item.description: After my favorite New York-style pizza place in town closed down (Pie Guy), I was on the lookout for a good pizza place. I heard of Bud's Pizza and Beer being…
item.content:encoded:
After my favorite New York-style pizza place in town closed down (Pie Guy), I was on the lookout for a good pizza place. I heard of Bud’s Pizza and Beer being comparable, so I went to check it out, and it did not disappoint! The ambiance is great, it has cozy vintage vibes, plenty of seating, and I’ve always had good service here.

The appetizers are all excellent. The wings are good, the meatballs are good, the beer nugs are good, and the homemade toasted ravioli is the best I’ve had in the entire Metro area.

Although I would consider the pizza more of just a standard “pizza” than New York style, the quality of the ingredients and the cook on the pizza are all top notch, and I highly recommend it as a place to take a group, get a bunch of apps, and share a pizza or two.

They recently removed Giardiniera from the menu though, which makes me sad.

item.title: Carl's Drive-In
item.description: Carl's Drive-In is a charming, no-frills diner right off historic route 66. It's cash only and seating is very limited, so it can get packed during peak hours.…
item.content:encoded:
Carl’s Drive-In is a charming, no-frills diner right off historic route 66. It’s cash only and seating is very limited, so it can get packed during peak hours. The menu is small and to the point - they do smash burgers to order, and they also have IBC root beer on tap. They also have what I think of as “Chicago tamales” on the menu, which I find delightful.

If you want a little taste of Americana, get an IBC root beer float, a double smash burger, and some fries.

I’d say it’s a solid smash burger, and it was my favorite in the area until I tried Woofies. Between the limited seating, limited hours, and being cash only, it can be kind of hard to find the right time to go, but it’s worth a visit.

item.title: El Jarocho
item.description: One of the first things I needed to find after moving to St. Louis was traditional Mexican food. Before I found El Jarocho I came across El Toluco (rip), a…
item.content:encoded:
One of the first things I needed to find after moving to St. Louis was traditional Mexican food. Before I found El Jarocho I came across El Toluco (rip), a similar Mexican grocery/taqueria combination that was close by, and they had awesome Al Pastor tacos - but unfortunately they closed down within a few months of finding it.

I’ll take any opportunity I can to talk up El Jarocho. Here you can find street tacos with corn tortillas, onions, cilantro, and meat, served with lime. The steak tacos are amazing, and the green sauce is top notch. My biggest complaint about El Jarocho is they don’t have Mexican rice or refried pinto beans - they have white rice and black beans.

My favorite item on the menu is the “Burrito nuevo”, which is a burrito filled with steak, queso fresco, and fries. It’s very similar to the California Burrito that you’ll find all over San Diego, just minus the guacamole.

This is a great taqueria/grocery store combo and I highly recommend you check it out. I’m going to keep looking for more good Mexican food, and I have many more places on my list to try, but El Jarocho is always going to be a staple.

item.title: Failoni's Restaurant
item.description: Recently, I saw pizzababble put Failoni's as his number one pizza place in the whole city, so I had to check it out. I've tried a few other places from his…
item.content:encoded:
Recently, I saw pizzababble put Failoni’s as his number one pizza place in the whole city, so I had to check it out. I’ve tried a few other places from his recommendations like “Providence by the Slice” in Kansas City and it was quite good. I figure few people have tried as many St. Louis-style pizzas as ol’ pizzababble so it’s worth a try.

I was impressed to learn that the building has been in operation since 1916 under the Failoni name. They also make their pizzas in a brick oven, which feels unique and also very St. Louis. I checked it out recently and we got toasted ravioli, salad, cheesy garlic bread, and two St. Louis-style pizzas. Overall, I thought it was okay. The toasted ravioli did not stand out, and I didn’t like the house salad, it was a bit too sweet for me.

The pizzas were pretty good, I liked that the sauce was not overly sweet and didn’t taste artificial. The crust was nice and crispy - they clearly perfected the low hydration, cracker crust made with yeast. It tasted very similar to when I made a St. Louis-style pizza at home with a three-day ferment, except theirs was crispier due to the brick oven cook.

Overall, it was a decent STL-style pizza, but it’s not in my top five. The patio was nice and it would be a good place to bring a few friends and have a drink.

item.title: Farotto's
item.description: Farotto's is a family-owned restaurant that has been making pizzas since 1956, making it one of the oldest ones as far as I can tell (Imo's began in 1964).…
item.content:encoded:
Farotto’s is a family-owned restaurant that has been making pizzas since 1956, making it one of the oldest ones as far as I can tell (Imo’s began in 1964). It’s my top-rated spot for St. Louis-style pizza - their pizza has an extra-extra-thin crust and has a buttery and flaky aspect to it that I haven’t experienced at any other pizza place. The sauce is slightly sweet but balanced, and blends well with the melted Provel.

Everything here is good - the toasted ravioli, the pizza, the pasta, the sandwiches. The STL sticks are their version of provel bites and it’s a standout item for me.

Farotto’s is also a great place to take a group, and it’s been one of my preferred restaurants to bring out-of-town guests. Their location in Rock Hill has an event space below, and a big open raised patio/restaurant on the upper level.

item.title: Grace Chicken + Fish
item.description: Grace is a classic comfort food spot to get fried chicken and sides. Grace used to have some competition in the fried chicken arena with Southern, a restaurant…
item.content:encoded:
Grace is a classic comfort food spot to get fried chicken and sides.

Grace used to have some competition in the fried chicken arena with Southern, a restaurant connected to Pappy’s, but it closed down. Most of the other chicken spots are chains like Chuck’s Hot Chicken and Dave’s Hot Chicken, neither of which I like that much. I have yet to try Hodak’s or Gus’s, the two other local spots I’ve heard of.

Although no one can compete with Prince’s in Nashville for me, I think Grace is pretty good. My biggest complaint is that the spice levels are very low - usually in Nashville I get medium or hot and I’m suffering a bit, but at Grace I can get the extra hot and still wish it had more spice. Aside from missing some heat, the flavor is great, the chicken is crispy, and the sides are good.

item.title: JJ Twig's Pizza & Pub
item.description: J.J. Twig's is the only place in town that I know of that specifically makes a Chicago thin-crust pizza. They also make a "double decker pizza" - two pizzas…
item.content:encoded:
J.J. Twig’s is the only place in town that I know of that specifically makes a Chicago thin-crust pizza. They also make a “double decker pizza” - two pizzas stacked on top of each other with the crusts braided together.

They have locations in Valley Park, O’Fallon, Southampton, and there’s even one in the Northern Chicago suburbs in Palatine, IL. I’ve been to the Valley Park and Southampton locations, and both have good food and good vibes. It’s a great place to bring a group and have a drink and some pizza. The toasted ravs are good, and it’s the best Italian beef I’ve had in St. Louis.

item.title: Kishimoto Mendo
item.description: As a long time fan of Menya Rui, I've been hyped to try Kishimoto Mendo ever since it was announced. Kishimoto Mendo is the new Tonkotsu-style ramen concept…
item.content:encoded:
As a long time fan of Menya Rui, I’ve been hyped to try Kishimoto Mendo ever since it was announced. Kishimoto Mendo is the new Tonkotsu-style ramen concept from the chef-owner of Menya Rui. Tonkotsu is my favorite style of ramen, so although the Shoyu at Menya Rui is fantastic, I wasn’t fully satisfied with the STL ramen scene.

We ended up going to Kishimoto Mendo during opening weekend, and it’s the best Tonkotsu ramen I’ve ever had, and I’ve had several across San Diego and Chicago (haven’t been to Tokyo yet, sadly). I really respect that the owner, Steven Pursley, delayed the opening until he was sure that the soup was up to his personal standards. We’ve been a few times and it’s been a complete 5/5 every time.

The wings are also good, though I prefer the karaage (fried chicken) at Menya Rui.

The pork broth is rich, flavorful, and comforting. The ramen shop vibes in the restaurant are great, and I love that it has twice as much seating as Menya Rui.

I highly recommend stopping by and getting the classic Tonkotsu ramen, and I would put Kishimoto Mendo on my list of “must try” restaurants in St. Louis.

item.title: La Pizza
item.description: La Pizza is one of the only places in St. Louis where you can get an authentic New York-style pizza. It's a small shop that is mostly set up for takeout with a…
item.content:encoded:
La Pizza is one of the only places in St. Louis where you can get an authentic New York-style pizza. It’s a small shop that is mostly set up for takeout with a few small tables for dining in.

The atmosphere is very much a friendly neighborhood joint and the vibes are truly 5/5. We showed up one night when they were busy with take out orders for the rest of the night, and they managed to fit us in and make us a fresh pizza and wings. We got a sausage and pepperoni pizza.

As much as I liked the place and the people, I thought the pizza was just okay. One thing is I’m not a fan of strips of sausage, which I know is just the way it’s often done with NY-style, so I need to learn my lesson and just get pepperoni (the midwest in me just always wants the bulk sausage on my pizza). The crust was a little bland to me. I thought it was an overall decent pizza, I just probably wouldn’t go out of my way for it.

item.title: La Tejana Taqueria
item.description: One of the first types of cuisine I was on the lookout for when I arrived in St. Louis was traditional Mexican food. I saw La Tejana come up frequently in…
item.content:encoded:
One of the first types of cuisine I was on the lookout for when I arrived in St. Louis was traditional Mexican food. I saw La Tejana come up frequently in recommendations.

Unfortunately, my experience did not live up to expectations. When I visited, I ordered steak tacos, but I got shredded meat and the order was pretty cold. There was no one else in the restaurant except one person on the Casino machines and it was silent aside from the dings from the machine.

It’s entirely possible I just visited at a very strange time and had a particularly bad experience that is not the norm, but I personally did not have a good experience during my visit.

item.title: Louie
item.description: Louie has good vibes, great food and an excellent location. It's right on the strip on DeMun Ave in Clayton next to Clementine's Naughty & Nice Ice Cream,…
item.content:encoded:
Louie has good vibes, great food and an excellent location. It’s right on the strip on DeMun Ave in Clayton next to Clementine’s Naughty & Nice Ice Cream, Sasha’s Wine Bar, and a few other shops and restaurants. I really enjoyed the atmosphere of the street, as I saw a lot of people eating on the patios, walking around, and kids riding their bikes, all with the backdrop of the greenery of Concordia Park. It felt very lively and energetic, and that’s what I love to see in St. Louis.

My partner and I went to Louie for an anniversary dinner and had a great time. The service was fantastic, as well as the food - particularly the bread and focaccia, a personal favorite. They also get burrata flown in from Italy, so that was a treat.

I also had the pizza, which I would probably rate a 4.5/5 - very good, but probably not the best in the whole city. Overall it was a great experience and a great place to go for a celebration.

item.title: Mac's Local Eats
item.description: Mac's Local Eats is a local smash burger spot in Dogtown. They really take the smash in smash burger seriously - it's almost a smear of burger with very crispy…
item.content:encoded:
Mac’s Local Eats is a local smash burger spot in Dogtown. They really take the smash in smash burger seriously - it’s almost a smear of burger with very crispy edges. If you like your smash burger extra thin and crispy, this is the place for you.

I liked the quality of the meat and flavor of the burger at Mac’s, but it’s was just a little too smashed for me personally. My choice for smash burgers in St. Louis would be Woofie’s or Carl’s, but I totally understand why people like Mac’s.

item.title: Menya Rui
item.description: Menya Rui was my first introduction to ramen in St. Louis, which was lucky for me since it's excellent. For a while, I went to Menya Rui once a week - even if…
item.content:encoded:
Menya Rui was my first introduction to ramen in St. Louis, which was lucky for me since it’s excellent.

For a while, I went to Menya Rui once a week - even if this meant waiting in line for two hours in the St. Louis heat, or waiting in the car during winter. This is a testament to how good the ramen Menya Rui is.

Shoyu ramen is the main focus at Menya Rui, and they do it very well. The broth is light yet has a deep flavor. I would also highly recommend the Karaage as an appetizer, which they’ve perfected as well.

As much as I love Menya Rui, Tonkotsu is my favorite type of ramen and I always felt sad that I couldn’t get it there and try their take on it. Fortunately for all of us, Kishimoto Mendo opened up recently in the Delmar Loop by the same chef-owner as Menya Rui, so now you can get both Shoyu and Tonkotsu on opposite ends of town.

item.title: Nicky Slices Pizza Club
item.description: I know St. Louis is the town of thin cracker-crust pizza, but I'm partial to the thicker, fluffier Detroit-style pie. When I first moved here, I tried Motor…
item.content:encoded:
I know St. Louis is the town of thin cracker-crust pizza, but I’m partial to the thicker, fluffier Detroit-style pie. When I first moved here, I tried Motor Town Pizza and the Detroit-style at the now defunct Pie Guy, but neither scratched the itch for me. Jet’s is a good option, but a chain is never going to be top-tier.

Nicky Slices Pizza Club has identified and filled the gap for an amazing Detroit-style pizza place with their location in The Hill. My recommendation is to get The Roner - a Detroit-style with cupped pepperoni and basil, drizzled with garlic chili hot honey.

I’ve also tried the thin crust, which is a beautiful combination of Chicago tavern and STL-style. It’s thin, savory, and amazing with giardiniera on top.

item.title: O'B Que's
item.description: Tucked away at a gas station in Chesterfield, O'B'Que's serves up Texas-style brisket and BBQ. I tried the ribs, brisket, and pulled pork, and all had a great…
item.content:encoded:
Tucked away at a gas station in Chesterfield, O’B’Que’s serves up Texas-style brisket and BBQ. I tried the ribs, brisket, and pulled pork, and all had a great wood-smoked flavor without being too overwhelmingly smokey. Best of all, they have a spicy vinegar BBQ sauce, my favorite.

My only complaint was that the brisket was a bit lean and dry, but I went 30 minutes before closing so I’m going to try again earlier on another day and hope I can get some of the point.

This has been the only place I’ve found so far that does Texas-style brisket, and is currently my favorite BBQ in town.

item.title: Pappy's Smokehouse
item.description: It's hard for me to properly rate Pappy's, because I'm a bit torn on it. On the one hand, they have a great spot, always a line and a lot of energy, they're…
item.content:encoded:
It’s hard for me to properly rate Pappy’s, because I’m a bit torn on it. On the one hand, they have a great spot, always a line and a lot of energy, they’re well known, and I love seeing that in St. Louis. I’d also say they have the best ribs in St. Louis - on par with or better than everything I’ve tried in Memphis, and by far the best in St. Louis. On the other hand, if you go to Pappy’s and order anything but the ribs, it’ll be pretty good but it won’t blow you away, and that might make you confused why they’re always at the top of every list in St. Louis.

The first time I went to Pappy’s, which was also one of my first BBQ experiences in St. Louis, I got brisket and a few sides. Pappy’s doesn’t really do Texas-style brisket, rather more of a thinly sliced brisket, which wasn’t what I was looking for. I also wasn’t a big fan of the fried corn, which I’ve never had before. Later I learned to order the ribs and it really blew me away.

Go to Pappy’s, get the ribs. They’re good.

item.title: Stacked STL
item.description: I've been to Stacked a couple of times, and it's always good. I'll admit that burgers just aren't my favorite food, and if I'm going to have a burger, I prefer…
item.content:encoded:
I’ve been to Stacked a couple of times, and it’s always good. I’ll admit that burgers just aren’t my favorite food, and if I’m going to have a burger, I prefer a smash burger (and Woofie’s is my favorite choice for that). So my personal rating might be a bit “stacked” against them (sorry).

As far as thick burgers go, Stacked is a very good one. You get to select all the ingredients and write them down in your Scantron test with your #2 pencil for bun, meat, cheese, toppings, etc. so the burger can be exactly what you want. Also they have a buffalo chicken toasted ravioli that I like a lot and plenty of local beers on tap. You can also go around the corner and get an ice cream sandwich at Sugarwitch.

Middle Eastern food in general is one of my favorite types of cuisine, and Lebanese in specific is possibly my favorite variation of it. I was excited to discover Taste of Lebanon right in Central West End.

The hummus, baba ganoush, and falafel at Taste of Lebanon are all fantastic - the best I’ve had in the St. Louis area. The lentil soup was also very good, and the various grilled meats are also good, though Sultan‘s kefta tops my list.

Taste of Lebanon also offers hookah and has a separate room for it, which I have not experienced but I think it’s cool that there’s a restaurant with both food and hookah available.

item.content:encoded:
Telva is a Balkan-inspired cafe from the owners of the famous Balkan Treat Box. I visited on the recommendation that it’s one of the best chai teas around, and I have to agree!

Telva’s all around a cool spot - the decor is very warm and inviting, and it’s in a walkable area close to a plant nursery and a few other cafes and restaurants like Olive + Oak and Le Macaron French Pastries. Telva also has breakfast/brunch items in addition to a full coffee bar. Many of the items on the menu have a Balkan flair to them, which is super unique.

I really loved going to this cafe and I’m excited to try more of the menu.

item.title: Vinnie's Italian Beef & Gyros
item.description: There's only a few places in all of St. Louis that do a rendition of an Italian beef sandwich, as seen in 4 Chicago-style Italian beef sandwiches in St. Louis…
item.content:encoded:
There’s only a few places in all of St. Louis that do a rendition of an Italian beef sandwich, as seen in 4 Chicago-style Italian beef sandwiches in St. Louis to satisfy fans of ‘The Bear’. I’ve tried most of the list (I haven’t been able to convince myself to try the Italian beef at Blues City Deli when the reuben is calling to me) but none taste quite like the real thing. The Italian beef to me is something that requires very few ingredients but a very specific process and execution, otherwise it’s simply not a beef, it’s a roast beef sandwich or french dip or something else.

I liked the neighborhood vibes at Vinnie’s, and this is an unpopular opinion, but I thought the beef was just okay. I was very excited to try it, but the giardiniera had olives in it and wasn’t spicy, it had mixed red and green peppers instead of just green, the au jus (usually called gravy) didn’t have much in the way of herbs and spices, and it had cheese on it by default. I would say it did not scratch the itch for an Italian beef that I have for me personally.

I did like the gyro from Vinnie’s and appreciate that the establishment exists. For anyone who has not had the chance to try an authentic beef before, I’d recommend my preference - dipped, double hot.

item.title: Woofies Hot Dogs

item.content:encoded:
There are three staple foods of the Chicagoan’s diet - the Italian beef sandwich, the Chicago-style hotdog, and deep dish pizza.

Travel only a few hours away, and not only do you stop seeing a hot dog and beef stand on every corner, but you don’t see them at all.

The ingredients on a Chicago dog are as follows:

  • Pickle spear
  • Tomato slice (2x)
  • Sport pepper (2x)
  • Relish, neon green
  • Onion, diced
  • Mustard
  • Celery salt
  • Poppyseed bun
  • Vienna Beef hotdog (steamed!)

None of these ingredients are optional or negotiable (unless you’re making a depression dog, but that’s another story).

I’m happy to report that not only does Woofie’s out in Overland not only make a good Chicago dog, but they make a perfect Chicago dog. On top of that, they make the best smash burger ever. If you’re looking for a good burger or dog in a no-frills joint that matches the vibe of your neighborhood corner hot dog stand in Chicago, head over to Woofie’s!

I’m only giving them a 4.5 instead of a 5 because I wasn’t a fan of the Italian beef sandwich they offered.
